providerDataContract.purpose: Create a short scene about a fictional game creature.

sharedPrompt.identity: Use the input image as the exact identity reference for this fictional creature. Preserve its face, silhouette, anatomy, colours, markings and life stage without redesigning it.
sharedPrompt.continuity: Wanderer-77 may appear only where the scene description requests the astronaut. Keep the creature as the clear subject and preserve the same creature identity for the whole shot.
sharedPrompt.motion: Use natural breathing, weight, blinking and purposeful body movement. Keep anatomy physically coherent with no morphing or duplicated parts.
sharedPrompt.camera: One continuous, stable cinematic wildlife shot with a slow low camera move, readable action and restrained depth of field.
sharedPrompt.world: The Fend is a warm, strange, habitable alien planet with living Current, damp terrain, moving air and practical environmental contact.
sharedPrompt.style: Premium live-action science-fantasy, emotionally warm and wondrous without becoming childish, cartoon-like or frightening.
sharedPrompt.exclusions: No dialogue, subtitles, logos, text, weapons, unrequested characters, transformation, pixel art, cartoon rendering, human children or real people. Only include another fictional creature when the authored action requests it.

moments.playerLabel: First steps in the Mythical Forest
moments.location: the Mythical Forest trail beyond the damaged Wanderer-77
moments.action: The creature takes two cautious steps onto bioluminescent forest ground, tests the living Current with one paw or contact limb, then looks back toward Wanderer-77, visible from behind at the edge of frame.
moments.trigger: Prepared after the first creature portrait is ready; first shown on Forest arrival if complete, otherwise delivered to the Creature Archive when ready.
moments.fallback: Immediate moving portrait tableau; gameplay never waits.

moments.location: the Project Beacon overlook at dusk, above a recovering region of the Fend
moments.action: The creature stands beside the quiet Beacon as living light travels from the landscape into it. Wanderer-77 watches from a separate position while considering the responsibility of returning to Earth.
moments.trigger: Prepared when the finale reflection begins and delivered immediately or through the Creature Archive when ready.
moments.fallback: Immediate moving portrait tableau; the ending remains playable.

moments.location: the newly opened rescue enclosure in the region just completed
moments.action: The creature approaches the opened enclosure, pauses so the freed guardian can choose, then leads it toward the distant warm lights of the Sanctuary. Wanderer-77 remains visible behind them without blocking either creature.
moments.trigger: Prepared as soon as the guardian rescue is confirmed, including when the resident-release panel owns the immediate screen.
moments.fallback: The authored rescue moment appears immediately; the generated scene arrives later in the Creature Archive.

moments.location: the Sanctuary beside living roots and established alien vegetation
moments.action: The creature and the welcomed Sanctuary resident exchange a calm recognition through posture, distance and a small mirrored movement. Wanderer-77 observes from a respectful separate position.
moments.trigger: Prepared when the resident trust event is recorded and delivered immediately or through the Creature Archive when ready.
moments.fallback: Immediate moving portrait tableau; Sanctuary interaction continues.

moments.location: a Sanctuary recovery overlook above the changed region
moments.action: The creature and the Sanctuary resident inspect the recovering region together. A visible environmental response acknowledges what their expedition changed while Wanderer-77 records the result from behind.
moments.trigger: Prepared when the resident expedition debrief is recorded and delivered immediately or through the Creature Archive when ready.
moments.fallback: Immediate moving portrait tableau; rewards and progression continue.
